subject: Convertible tranche proposal + sprint-aligned renewal structure
messages:
From: Marta Alvarez <marta@cartesia.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Hughes <ben.hughes@cartesia.ai>
Date: 2028-07-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal coming up — can we make term more flexible?

Rishi,

Thanks for the continued partnership — renewal for our account hits in September and our finance and product teams are pushing for a structure that gives us predictable committed capacity while allowing flexibility across quarters. High-level asks: 

- Can we split next-year commitment into convertible tranches (Q1 reserve + two optional tranches) so we can bring forward spend if usage ramps?
- We want sprint-aligned top-ups (monthly/quarterly triggers tied to product launches) rather than a single annual true-up.
- Optional auto-renew for the base tranche only; optional tranches should require explicit opt-in.

Attached is a quick sketch of what procurement prefers. Can your team put together 2–3 workable structures (financial and billing cadence) and call out any limits on burst or spike protection?

Appreciate it — Marta

Attachments: Cartesia-Renewal-Sketch.pdf (stub)

--
Marta Alvarez
Head of Infrastructure
Cartesia Inc.

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Marta Alvarez <marta@cartesia.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — can we make term more flexible?

Marta — thanks for the clear brief. This is a scenario we’ve structured before and we can absolutely propose options that balance predictability and flexibility. At a glance, three pragmatic pathways we can model: 

1) Anchored base + two convertible tranches
   - Year 1 base commitment (co-term with existing contract) that auto-renews by default unless opted out.
   - Two optional tranches (mid-year and end-year) which Cartesia can elect to convert into committed usage within 30 days of the trigger.
   - Billing: base billed monthly; converted tranche billed monthly after conversion.

2) Quarterly sprint-topup with capped burst protection
   - Base annual commitment spread monthly for predictability.
   - Sprint-topups processed as monthly purchase orders up to predefined cap; any use beyond cap triggers overage rate.
   - Option for limited carry-forward of unused topup credits for one quarter.

3) Hybrid convertible + runway credits (recommended for high-variance product schedules)
   - Smaller base to keep auto-renew simple.
   - Convertible tranches sized to match product sprints (e.g., 3-month bundles).
   - Include pre-funded runway credits (applied to first spikes) to smooth billing and avoid emergency true-up.

Operational notes / constraints:
- Burst protection: we can set a safety fallback to a lower-capacity model when usage exceeds the highest committed tranche; full traffic won’t be blocked, but latency guarantees temporarily relax.
- Legal/pricing: tranches that are "convertible into committed spend" will need SOW language and a brief amendment for billing cadence.
- Lead time: converting a tranche to committed typically needs 7 business days for capacity planning if it requires dedicated GPU pools.

I attached a working matrix (Cartesia-Convertible-Tranche-Options-v2.pdf) and a draft SOW worksheet (SOW-Tranche-Matrix.xlsx) for your review.

Can we set a sync Friday 9am PT to walk through the three options and surface any procurement must-haves? I’ll loop in Marissa (CS lead) to confirm on onboarding/ops and Camila for SOW redline guidance.

Thanks — Rishi

Attachments: Cartesia-Convertible-Tranche-Options-v2.pdf (stub); SOW-Tranche-Matrix.xlsx (stub)

--
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Lead, Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Marta Alvarez <marta@cartesia.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-04T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — can we make term more flexible?

Marta — quick ops perspective:

- Implementation checklist: if you opt into a tranche mid-year, we’ll need the committed token volumes, desired latency SLO, and whether you require dedicated capacity. That determines whether we provision from Dedicated pools (7–10 business days) or host on shared capacity (usually 48–72 hours).
- Billing flow suggestion: base monthly invoice + a separate line for converted tranche(s) to keep forecasts clean. If Cartesia wants quarterly invoicing for tranches, we can do that but it will affect forecast smoothing for both sides.
- Pilot recommendation: convert a single small tranche as a trial in Q1 to validate capacity routing and KC cache behavior during sprints.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for ingestion, cache priming, and ops escalation that maps to the three options Rishi outlined. If Camila is good with the SOW framing, we can push a draft amendment to procurement after Friday’s sync.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Marta Alvarez <marta@cartesia.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-06T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — can we make term more flexible?

Marta — thanks, team. Legal/RevOps notes before our sync: 

- Draft SOW language: we’ll use "convertible tranche" language that requires a 30-day written election and sets the effective converted date as the first of the following month. This keeps billing clean and gives us capacity lead time.
- Auto-renew clause: limit auto-renew to the anchored base tranche only. Optional tranches must be opted into explicitly each fiscal year.
- Cancellation/early-exit: converted tranches will have a 90-day minimum committed period to avoid churn/operational churn.
- Credits: propose a runway-credit pool (pre-funded) that can be consumed for spikes; unused credits can be applied toward future converted tranche billing, not refunded.

I’ll prepare a redline of the standard renewal amendment and an SOW appendix with the tranche matrix. If those look ok, Rishi — can you sign off on the business structure so I can send for procurement review on Monday?

Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
